content.text: I couldn't see the JWT strategy in the retrieved snippets, so this diagnosis is partly inferred. I also had no way to open files here. The symptom narrows it down: login and refresh succeed, so tokens are being issued. Only validation of the access token fails. That points to the access token being signed differently from how it is verified.

candidates.explanation: This method builds the access and refresh tokens for both login and refresh. Login and refresh succeed, so tokens are issued. A likely defect is that the access token is signed with the wrong secret or expiry (for example the refresh secret, or an expiry already in the past). It could also carry a payload that the strategy rejects, such as a missing or misnamed `id` or `sessionId`. The JWT access strategy would then fail verification on every protected request. I couldn't see the method body, so the exact line is inferred.

This strategy verifies the access token on protected routes. If its `secretOrKey` config key differs from the one used to sign the access token, or `validate` rejects a valid payload (wrong field check, or `ignoreExpiration` and `expiresIn` mishandled), every request gets 401. The file wasn't in the retrieved snippets, so the line range is a guess.

fix.description: In getTokensData, sign the access token with the access-token secret (`auth.secret`) and `auth.expires`, and include `{ id, role, sessionId }` in the payload. Make sure JwtStrategy uses the same `auth.secret` as `secretOrKey` and that validate accepts that payload. Keep the refresh token on `auth.refreshSecret` and `auth.refreshExpires`.
